structured_output.hypothesis: If present ocean basins have been ocean since the earliest Silurian (about 443 Ma), the present sea floor should contain a substantial share of crust of Palaeozoic or early Secondary age, rather than only young crust.
structured_output.pass_criterion: At least 25% of the area of the present ocean-floor age grid has a crustal age of 250 Ma or more, and the maximum grid age is at least 250 Ma. That would show that ocean floor of Palaeozoic or earliest Mesozoic age underlies today's oceans, as Darwin's inference implies.
structured_output.fail_criterion: Less than 5% of the area of the ocean-floor age grid has a crustal age of 250 Ma or more, and the maximum grid age is below 250 Ma. That would show that the present sea floor is wholly post-Palaeozoic, so the present oceans did not exist as ocean floor from the Silurian.
structured_output.interpretation: Darwin's 'oceanic islands bear no Palaeozoic or Secondary formations' becomes the age of present oceanic lithosphere. His 'oceans have extended from the remotest period' becomes the idea that present ocean-floor area is old crust, and his 'Secondary' means Mesozoic. The test is a modern reinterpretation. Subduction destroys old sea floor, so absence of old crust does not prove that no ocean was there. Even so, the test directly refutes any claim that these specific ocean basins are Silurian-age features. Darwin's second clause, about continents being long-lived land, is not tested here. The grid age field is in millions of years (Ma). Area-weighted percentages are computed over all non-null ocean cells.
